name: Fetal Parvovirus Syndrome
aliases: Hydrops Fetalis due to Parvovirus B19

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Parvovirus B19 Congenital Infection Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of non-immune hydrops fetalis detected by ultrasound
Detection of parvovirus B19 DNA by PCR in fetal or neonatal blood or tissue
Evidence of fetal anemia demonstrated by Doppler ultrasonography or fetal blood sampling
Maternal seroconversion or positive IgM antibodies to parvovirus B19 during pregnancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hydrops fetalis with detection of parvovirus B19 DNA in fetal/neonatal samples or evidence of fetal anemia with maternal seroconversion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on ultrasound findings combined with virological confirmation.

laboratory: Detection of parvovirus B19 DNA by PCR in fetal blood or tissue
imaging: Ultrasound evidence of hydrops fetalis (ascites, pleural and pericardial effusions, skin edema)
Elevated middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity on Doppler ultrasound
Fetal echocardiography showing myocarditis or cardiac dysfunction
genetic: No specific genetic mutations; diagnosis based on viral detection
other: Histopathological evidence of viral inclusions in fetal tissues
Placental inflammation consistent with parvovirus infection

distinguishingFeatures: Hydrops fetalis without evidence of parvovirus B19 infection
Other infectious or genetic causes identified
Hydrops fetalis due to red cell alloimmunization

redFlags: Rapid development of non-immune hydrops fetalis
Severe fetal anemia with signs of cardiac failure
references: Anderson MJ, et al. Parvovirus B19 infection in pregnancy: diagnosis and management. Obstet Gynecol. 2020.
Heegaard ED, Brown KE. Human parvovirus B19. Clin Microbiol Rev. 2002.
Orphanet: Fetal parvovirus syndrome. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
